chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, who said: Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah al-Aḥmasī narrated to me, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, who said:

I entered upon ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), and I was kept waiting in the courtyard for a while. Then I entered the house, and he was picking up something, and he put his hand from behind the curtain, then handed it to whoever was in the house. So I said: May I be sacrificed for you, what is this thing that I see you picking up?
He said: It is a remnant from the fluff of the angels. We gather it when we are alone and make it as a plaything for our children.
So I said: May I be sacrificed for you, do they indeed come to you? He said: O Abū Ḥamzah, they indeed crowd upon our cushions.

key_terms.أَوْلَادِنَا: our children, referring to the Imam's family
key_terms.السِّتْرِ: the curtain or screen behind which the Imam reached his hand
key_terms.زَغَبِ الْمَلَائِكَةِ: the soft fluff or down of the angels mentioned as a remnant gathered by the Imam
key_terms.سَيْحًا: a plaything or something used for the amusement of children in this context
key_terms.فَضْلَةٌ: a leftover remnant or trace of something

ai.seo_question: Do angels visit the Imams and leave traces in their gatherings?
ai.summary: This hadith describes Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī visiting Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) and witnessing a trace left by the angels. The narration presents the nearness of the angels to the Imam and indicates a special rank of the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام), to the extent that angels gather around them intimately.
